abstract: Directs analytical instrument calibrations, forensic spectral validation, and mass spectrometric dwell times
system_message:
You are the Analytical Chemistry Director (CHM). Your role is to direct analytical instrument calibrations, forensic spectral validation, and mass spectrometric dwell times, as well as to oversee sample archive preservation.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Directs analytical instrument calibrations, forensic spectral validation, and mass spectrometric dwell times（SPEC）
information_points.content:
CHM-SPEC-ON9：For High-throughput metagenomic shotgun profiling, the forensic spectrometric calibration is verified for the multi-collector analytical instrumentation dedicated to tracer isotope detection under ISO/IEC 17025 forensic standards, while the laboratory desolvation dwell time during analyte preparation is 25 min.
CHM-SPEC-9W9：For Continuous isotopic ratio mass spectrometry, the multi-collector analytical instrumentation dedicated to tracer isotope detection has its forensic spectrometric calibration verified according to ISO/IEC 17025 forensic standards, and the laboratory desolvation dwell time in the secondary ionization and nebulizer vacuum chamber during analyte preparation is 35 min.
CHM-SPEC-LPG：For the Fluorescent nanoparticle dye-tracing array, forensic spectrometric calibration is not verified for the multi-collector analytical instrumentation dedicated to tracer isotope detection under ISO/IEC 17025 standards, and the laboratory desolvation dwell time in the nebulizer vacuum chamber is 15 min.

information_points.title: Sample archive preservation（ARCH）
information_points.content:
CHM-ARCH-WAL：For Continuous isotopic ratio mass spectrometry, the cryogenic sample storage capacity in the ultra-low temperature forensic containment unit at minus 80 degrees Celsius is 1000 samples for long-term evidentiary hold.
CHM-ARCH-OTP：For the Fluorescent nanoparticle dye-tracing array, the cryogenic sample storage capacity within the ultra-low temperature forensic containment unit at minus 80 degrees Celsius is 750 samples for long-term evidentiary hold.
CHM-ARCH-O17：For High-throughput metagenomic shotgun profiling, the cryogenic sample storage capacity in the ultra-low temperature forensic containment unit at minus 80 degrees Celsius is 500 samples for long-term evidentiary hold.
